conditions: deterministic algorithms against a distribution over instances

source.label: thm:lb
source.quote: There exists a distribution over instances of the increasing bandits problem where no deterministic algorithm can achieve expected reward greater than $3 \, \OPT/\sqrt{k}$.

results.notes: Expression is the lower bound on the competitive ratio OPT/E[ALG] implied (E[ALG] <= 3 OPT/sqrt(k)). Comparator is the best single-arm policy (policy-regret style).

source.label: cor:lb-randalg
source.quote: For any randomized algorithm, there exists an instance for which its approximation factor is at least  $\sqrt{k}/3$.

results.notes: Via Yao's principle. Quantity is approximation factor (competitive ratio).

symbols.c_2: constant c_2>1 such that m lies in [f*(T-k)/c_2, f*(T-k)]

tuning: run with T-k as its horizon parameter

source.label: thm:alg1approx
source.quote: If $m \in [\frac{1}{c_2} f^*(T-k), f^*(T-k)]$ and $T \geq 2k$, then Algorithm~\ref{alg:rrr}, run with $T-k$ as its parameter ``$T$'', receives expected reward at least $\frac{\OPT_T}{8 c_2\gk}$ in $T$ steps.

results.notes: Expression is the competitive ratio OPT_T/E[ALG] upper bound.

source.label: thm:generalresult
source.quote: When $T > 4k\,,$ picking the parameter $m$ required by Algorithm~\ref{alg:rrr} using the procedure detailed in Algorithm~\ref{alg:get-mhat} with parameter $T_\text{pred} = \frac{T}{2} - k$ and running Algorithm~\ref{alg:rrr} with that value $\hat{m}$ achieves expected reward $ALG =\Omega(\OPT/(\sqrt{k} \log k))\,.$

results.notes: Competitive ratio O(sqrt(k) log k). Proof gives explicit constant (3+log(4k))*256*sqrt(k).

source.label: lemma:unknownT
source.quote: Suppose we run the procedure described in Algorithm~\ref{alg:Tuk}. If $T > 4k\,,$ then the reward achieved is at least $\frac{\OPT_T}{8192 \gk \log(128k)}$.

results.notes: Expression is competitive ratio bound; reward presumably in expectation over algorithm randomness.

symbols.beta_I: Concavity Envelope Exponent of the instance

conditions: instance has Concavity Envelope Exponent beta_I (every arm satisfies f_i(t) >= f_i(T)(t/T)^beta)

source.label: thm:ptrr-alpha
source.quote: Given an IMAB instance $I$ with Concavity Envelope Exponent $\beta_I$. If $T \ge 2k$, then $PTRR_\alpha$ for $\alpha \in (\beta_I, 1)$  with $\tau =T-k$, $m = \frac{\tau}{T} f^*(T)$  achieves $$\mathbb{E}[\text{reward from PTRR}_\alpha] \ge \frac{1}{2^{\alpha+3}(\alpha + 1)} \cdot \frac{\text{OPT}_T}{(k + 1)^{\frac{\alpha}{\alpha + 1}}},$$ Equivalently, the competitive ratio is $O(k^{\alpha/(\alpha+1)})$.

results.notes: Competitive ratio bound. Requires knowledge of f*(T) and choosing alpha > beta_I.

symbols.beta_e: Concavity Envelope Exponent beta in (0,1] of the hard instance

conditions: instance has Concavity Envelope Exponent beta_I = beta

source.quote: Fix $\beta \in (0, 1]$ and $k \ge 2$. For every (possibly randomized) algorithm, for $T$ sufficiently large, there exists an instance with Concavity Envelope Exponent $\beta_I = \beta$ such that $\frac{\mathbb{E}[\text{ALG}_T]}{\text{OPT}_T} \le C_\beta k^{-\beta/(\beta+1)},$ with $C_\beta = \frac{3}{2}(\beta + 1)^2 \left[\beta(\beta + 1)\right]^{-\beta/(\beta+1)}$.

results.notes: Expression is the lower bound on competitive ratio OPT/E[ALG].
